summary: Kaniksu NF ridge site: 1915 camp, 1926 log cabin, 1938 L-4 tower; only ruins by the 1950s, with footings and remnants still on the ridge.

facts.design: Log cabin with two platform towers (1926); 20-foot wooden tower with L-4 cab (1938)
facts.status_note: Only ruins by the 1950s; an undated visitor's account reports footings and remnants on the ridge, not standing structures

access.note: On Kaniksu National Forest land, reached on foot; the trail is unsigned

visit.trail_note: About 11 miles round trip with roughly 1,500 feet of gain; an unsigned trail climbs the south ridge to the sites

events.note: Log cabin built, with two platform towers about a mile apart (register); built by mop-up crews after the 1926 burn (WillhiteWeb)
Lawrence McKay completed a lookout station on Grassy Top and started one on Slumber Peak (Newport Miner, quoted by WashingtonLookouts; WillhiteWeb)
20-foot wooden tower with L-4 cab, half a mile southwest of the 1926 cabin
Only ruins remained 'by the 1950s' per the sources; exact year of decline not given

evidence.supports: lookout camp set up in 1915, replaced in 1926 by a log cabin with two platform towers about a mile apart
evidence.quote: A camp set up in 1915 was replaced in 1926 with a log cabin with 2 platform towers 1 mile apart on the north and southeast points.
In 1915, there was a lookout camp.

evidence.supports: 1926 cabin built by mop-up crews after the 1926 burn
evidence.quote: In 1926, a log cabin was built by mop-up crews during the final days of the huge 1926 burn which ravaged Pend Oreille County.
In 1931, Roy Mackay was struck by lightning.

evidence.supports: Newport newspaper reports McKay completed a lookout station on Grassy Top in 1932
evidence.quote: Lawrence McKay has completed a lookout station for the Forest Service on Grassy Top

evidence.supports: September 1932 completion of a station and start of another on Slumber Peak
evidence.quote: In 1932, September, Lawrence McKay finished the lookout station for the Forest Service on Grassy Top and starting work on another on Slumber Peak.

evidence.supports: 1938 20-foot wooden L-4 tower built half a mile southwest of the 1926 cabin
evidence.quote: In 1938 a 20' wooden L-4 tower was built 1/2 mile southwest of the 1926 cabin.

evidence.supports: 1938 20-foot wooden L-4 tower half a mile southwest of the 1926 cabin (firelookout.com)
evidence.quote: 1938: 20' wooden L-4 tower 1/2 mile southwest of 1926 cabin.

evidence.supports: footings and the most remnants at the southwest peak
evidence.quote: The SW peak has footings and the most remnants

administered by the U.S. Forest Service

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register dates the cabin to 1926 and the L-4 tower to 1938. A 1932 newspaper item says a lookout station was completed that year. The sources do not say whether that station was the 1926 cabin or a later building, so the story gives both dates.

The brief holds two coordinate sets roughly a kilometre apart. This record keeps the FFLOS register point (48.76621, -117.14505), which the register's own page supports; the other set is not in the sources cited here.

notes_for_editor: Dates disagree: register 1926 cabin and 1938 tower versus a 1932 newspaper station. Two names appear: Roy Mackay (struck by lightning, 1931) and Lawrence McKay (completed a station on Grassy Top, 1932). WillhiteWeb does not call Mackay a lookout. The story keeps the names separate and does not say they are one person. Brief elevation 1893.7 m matches the register's 6,213 ft. WillhiteWeb page is undated in the cache. No source gives a visit date for the ruins.
